title: The Cousin Who Spoke Before a King
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] When the persecution in Makkah became unbearable, a small group of Muslims fled across the sea to Abyssinia, hoping a distant king might protect them.
Narrator: [serious] Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's own cousin, was chosen to lead them, even though he had no formal experience speaking to royalty.
Narrator: [reflective] The Quraysh, however, refused to let the matter rest, and they sent two clever envoys to the Negus, demanding the refugees be returned.
Narrator: [tense] If the king had listened only to those envoys, the entire group might have been sent back to face torture and possible death.
Narrator: [calm] Instead, the Negus asked to hear directly from the Muslims themselves, and it was Ja'far who stood to answer on their behalf.
Narrator: [with feeling] He described their old life honestly, admitting that before Islam they had worshipped idols and treated the weak with real cruelty.
Narrator: [warmly] Then he explained how the Prophet had taught them to pray, to speak truthfully, and to protect orphans instead of exploiting them.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Despite the pressure surrounding him, Ja'far spoke with a calmness that surprised everyone watching, as though the outcome no longer frightened him.
Narrator: [serious] The envoys then accused the Muslims of insulting Jesus, hoping this final claim would finally turn the Christian king against them.
Narrator: [with feeling] Ja'far recited verses about Jesus from the Quran, and as he spoke, the Negus reportedly wept until his beard grew wet with tears.
Narrator: [with wonder] Moved beyond expectation, the king declared that the teaching came from the same divine source as his own faith, and he refused to hand them over.
Narrator: [reflective] As a result, the small community remained safely in Abyssinia for years, protected by a ruler who had never even met the Prophet.
Narrator: [warmly] Years later, Ja'far finally reunited with the Prophet, who reportedly said he did not know which pleased him more, seeing Ja'far or hearing of that victory.
Narrator: [sadly] Ja'far was later killed at the Battle of Mu'tah, fighting until both his arms were lost, refusing to let the banner touch the ground.
Narrator: [with admiration] Whenever I read this story, I remember that quiet, honest words, spoken without fear, can move even the most powerful listener.

quiz.question: Why did a group of Muslims flee to Abyssinia?
options: Because persecution in Makkah had become unbearable
quiz.explanation: The narrator explains they fled because persecution in Makkah had become unbearable, hoping the king would protect them.

quiz.question: What might have happened if the Negus had only listened to the Quraysh envoys?
options: The refugees might have been sent back to face torture
The Muslims would have been rewarded
quiz.explanation: If the king had listened only to the envoys, the group might have been sent back to face torture and possible death.

quiz.question: What accusation did the envoys make about Jesus?
options: That the Muslims ignored him completely
quiz.explanation: The envoys accused the Muslims of insulting Jesus, hoping to turn the Christian king against them.

quiz.question: How did the Negus react when Ja'far recited verses about Jesus?
options: He wept until his beard was wet with tears
quiz.explanation: As Ja'far spoke, the Negus reportedly wept until his beard grew wet with tears.

quiz.question: How did Ja'far die at the Battle of Mu'tah?
options: He fought until both his arms were lost, refusing to drop the banner
quiz.explanation: Ja'far was killed fighting until both his arms were lost, refusing to let the banner touch the ground.

title: A Podcast on Nusaybah's Courage at Uhud
script: Host: [warmly] Welcome back to the show. Today my guest is Ridwan, who studies the roles women played in the earliest battles of Islam. Thanks for joining me.
Guest: [pleasantly] Thank you for having me. Nusaybah bint Ka'ab is a figure I could discuss for hours without running out of material.
Host: [curious] I've heard she is remembered mainly for the Battle of Uhud. What exactly did she do there?
Guest: [thoughtful] She originally went to the battlefield to give water to the wounded, not expecting to fight at all that day.
Guest: [serious] However, when the battle suddenly turned chaotic and enemy soldiers surrounded the Prophet, she picked up a sword without hesitation.
Host: [surprised] So she went from carrying water to defending the Prophet directly? That's a remarkable shift in just a few moments.
Guest: [nodding] Exactly, and despite receiving several serious wounds herself, she kept fighting, positioning her own body between the Prophet and the attackers.
Host: [impressed] Did the Prophet ever acknowledge what she had done that day?
Guest: [warmly] He did, and later he reportedly said that wherever he looked during the worst moments, he saw Nusaybah defending him.
Host: [thoughtful] That's an extraordinary compliment, especially considering how many soldiers were fighting around him at the same time.
Guest: [reflective] It is, and if she hadn't acted so quickly, some historians argue the outcome of that chaotic moment could have been far worse.
Host: [curious] Did her courage end after that particular battle, or did she continue serving afterward?
Guest: [explaining] She continued for years, even losing a hand in a later battle, yet she never stopped supporting the community she believed in.
Host: [moved] It sounds like her story challenges the idea that only men shaped those early, dangerous years of Islam.
Guest: [firmly] Precisely. Even though history often focuses on male commanders, Nusaybah's bravery proves that assumption was never entirely accurate.
Host: [warmly] Thank you, Ridwan, for reminding us of a courage that deserves far more recognition than it usually receives.
Guest: [smiling] Thank you for having me. I hope her story inspires listeners to look closer at the women behind these events.

quiz.question: Why did Nusaybah originally go to the battlefield at Uhud?
options: To give water to the wounded
quiz.explanation: The guest explains she originally went to give water to the wounded, not expecting to fight.

quiz.question: What made her pick up a sword?
options: The battle turned chaotic and enemies surrounded the Prophet
quiz.explanation: When the battle suddenly turned chaotic and enemies surrounded the Prophet, she picked up a sword without hesitation.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet reportedly say about Nusaybah?
options: That wherever he looked during the worst moments, he saw her defending him
That she should have stayed home
quiz.explanation: He reportedly said that wherever he looked during the worst moments, he saw Nusaybah defending him.

quiz.question: What happened to Nusaybah in a later battle?
quiz.explanation: She continued for years, even losing a hand in a later battle, yet never stopped supporting the community.

quiz.question: What is the guest's main point about Nusaybah's story?
options: That only men mattered in early Islam
That her bravery challenges the idea that only men shaped those dangerous years
That her story is not important
quiz.explanation: The guest argues Nusaybah's bravery proves that focusing only on male commanders was never entirely accurate.

title: The Merchant Who Refused Free Land
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] When Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf migrated to Madinah, he arrived with nothing, having left his entire fortune behind in Makkah.
Narrator: [warmly] A local resident generously offered to split his own house and wealth in half, insisting Abdur-Rahman simply take whatever he needed.
Narrator: [reflective] Most people in his position might have accepted gratefully, yet Abdur-Rahman politely declined, asking instead to be shown the way to the market.
Narrator: [thoughtful] That single request revealed something essential about his character, since he clearly preferred earning through honest effort over receiving charity.
Narrator: [with admiration] Within a remarkably short time, his careful trading had transformed his situation, and he became one of the wealthiest men in the community.
Narrator: [serious] However, unlike many wealthy merchants throughout history, he never allowed that fortune to soften his sense of responsibility toward others.
Narrator: [with feeling] Whenever caravans of his goods arrived in Madinah, he reportedly gave away enormous portions immediately, sometimes keeping barely anything for himself.
Narrator: [reflective] On one occasion, he donated an entire caravan of seven hundred loaded camels, an amount that shook the whole city that day.
Narrator: [thoughtful] If his wealth had come from anything questionable, such generosity might have seemed like an attempt to hide guilt, but that was never the case.
Narrator: [warmly] Everyone who dealt with him testified that his trading remained scrupulously honest, even when dishonesty would have earned him more.
Narrator: [with wonder] He once said that he feared his own wealth might become a test he would fail, so he kept giving it away deliberately.
Narrator: [serious] Despite his enormous riches, he lived modestly, choosing simple clothing and food rather than displaying the luxury he could easily afford.
Narrator: [reflective] In spite of his generosity, he never sought recognition for it, preferring that his charity remain quiet rather than publicly celebrated.
Narrator: [warmly] Abdur-Rahman's story reminds me that wealth itself is neutral, and what truly matters is the character of the hand that holds it.

quiz.question: What did Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf do when offered half of a resident's wealth?
options: He politely declined and asked to be shown the market instead
He refused to speak to the man
quiz.explanation: He politely declined the generous offer, asking instead to be shown the way to the market.

quiz.question: How did Abdur-Rahman become wealthy?
quiz.explanation: His careful trading transformed his situation, making him one of the wealthiest men in the community.

quiz.question: What did he do with the caravan of seven hundred camels?
options: He gave it to his family only
quiz.explanation: He donated an entire caravan of seven hundred loaded camels, an amount that shook the whole city.

quiz.question: Why did Abdur-Rahman say he kept giving his wealth away?
options: He feared his wealth might become a test he would fail
quiz.explanation: He said he feared his own wealth might become a test he would fail, so he gave it away deliberately.

quiz.question: How did Abdur-Rahman live despite his enormous riches?
options: Modestly, with simple clothing and food
quiz.explanation: Despite his enormous riches, he lived modestly, choosing simple clothing and food over displayed luxury.

title: Two Coworkers Discuss Khalid's Change of Command
script: Dewi: [thoughtful] Fajar, I finally read about Khalid ibn al-Walid last night, and one part of his story surprised me more than the battles did.
Fajar: [curious] I only know him as a brilliant military commander. What part surprised you?
Dewi: [reflective] Well, before becoming Muslim, he had actually commanded the army that defeated the Muslims at Uhud, largely through his own tactics.
Fajar: [surprised] Wait, so the man who later led Muslim armies once defeated them himself? That's a striking reversal.
Dewi: [nodding] Exactly, and once he accepted Islam, the Prophet gave him the title Sword of Allah, since his skill on the battlefield was undeniable.
Fajar: [thoughtful] I imagine that title brought both respect and pressure, considering how much everyone would now expect from him.
Dewi: [warmly] It did, and for years he won victory after victory, never losing a single battle he personally commanded.
Fajar: [interested] So what was the part that actually surprised you, then, if not the winning streak?
Dewi: [reflective] It was what happened later, when the caliph Umar removed him from his position as commander, even though Khalid was clearly still capable.
Fajar: [wincing] That sounds humiliating, especially after everything Khalid had achieved for the community over so many years.
Dewi: [thoughtful] You would expect that, but instead of protesting or resigning in anger, Khalid simply continued fighting as an ordinary soldier.
Fajar: [impressed] He stayed even after losing his rank? Most people in his position would have walked away entirely.
Dewi: [warmly] That's exactly why scholars admire this moment as much as his victories, since it revealed something about his priorities.
Fajar: [reflective] If his loyalty had truly depended on his title, he would have left immediately once that title disappeared.
Dewi: [smiling] Precisely. He once said that he fought for the cause, not for Umar's approval, and I think that line explains everything.
Fajar: [thoughtful] It's a strong reminder that real dedication survives even when recognition doesn't.

quiz.question: What had Khalid ibn al-Walid done before becoming Muslim?
options: He commanded the army that defeated the Muslims at Uhud
He was a trader in Madinah
quiz.explanation: Before becoming Muslim, he had commanded the army that defeated the Muslims at Uhud.

quiz.question: What title did the Prophet give Khalid after his conversion?
quiz.explanation: The Prophet gave him the title Sword of Allah, since his battlefield skill was undeniable.

quiz.question: What did the caliph Umar do to Khalid later?
options: He removed him from his position as commander
quiz.explanation: Umar removed Khalid from his position as commander, even though he was clearly still capable.

quiz.question: How did Khalid react to losing his command?
options: He continued fighting as an ordinary soldier
quiz.explanation: Instead of protesting or resigning, Khalid simply continued fighting as an ordinary soldier.

quiz.question: What did Khalid say explained his continued loyalty?
options: He fought for the cause, not for Umar's approval
quiz.explanation: He said he fought for the cause, not for Umar's approval, which Fajar and Dewi see as explaining his loyalty.

title: The Profitable Deal of Suhayb ar-Rumi
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Suhayb was captured as a child and sold repeatedly between different masters, which is why he grew up known simply as Suhayb the Roman.
Narrator: [reflective] Despite that difficult beginning, he eventually gained his freedom and built a genuinely successful trading business through years of patient effort.
Narrator: [warmly] When he embraced Islam, he faced the same hostility as other early believers, yet he remained firm even as pressure increased around him.
Narrator: [serious] Eventually, he decided he had to migrate to Madinah, since staying in Makkah had become too dangerous for someone openly practicing this new faith.
Narrator: [tense] However, as he prepared to leave, a group of Quraysh horsemen caught up with him just outside the city, blocking his path entirely.
Narrator: [calm] They told him plainly that he had arrived poor and had grown wealthy only because of them, so leaving with that wealth was unacceptable.
Narrator: [thoughtful] If he had refused their demand, the situation might have turned violent immediately, since the men were clearly prepared to fight him.
Narrator: [with feeling] Instead, Suhayb offered a calm proposal, telling them exactly where his money and gold were buried if they would simply let him pass unharmed.
Narrator: [with wonder] They agreed, and Suhayb walked away toward Madinah with nothing material left, having traded his entire fortune for the freedom to practice his faith.
Narrator: [warmly] When he finally reached Madinah and told the Prophet what had happened, the Prophet reportedly smiled and said that Suhayb had made a profitable deal.
Narrator: [reflective] That single sentence reframed the whole story, since what looked like total loss was actually described as the wisest transaction of his life.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Years later, Suhayb remained known for his generosity, often sharing food freely with anyone nearby, as though wealth had never truly mattered to him.
Narrator: [with admiration] Even in old age, he was chosen to lead the community in prayer during a moment of political uncertainty, a sign of deep trust.
Narrator: [warmly] Whenever I feel attached to something I might lose, I remember Suhayb at that gate, choosing faith over fortune without a trace of regret.

quiz.question: Why was Suhayb known as Suhayb the Roman?
options: He was captured as a child and sold repeatedly between masters
He traveled to Rome for trade
quiz.explanation: He was captured as a child and sold repeatedly, which is why he grew up known as Suhayb the Roman.

quiz.question: What did the Quraysh horsemen demand outside the city?
options: That he stay in Makkah forever
That he leave his wealth behind if he wanted to pass unharmed
That he convert back to his old religion
quiz.explanation: They told him leaving with his wealth was unacceptable, so he offered to tell them where it was buried in exchange for safe passage.

quiz.question: What did Suhayb offer the horsemen?
options: To tell them where his money and gold were buried
quiz.explanation: Suhayb offered a calm proposal, telling them exactly where his money and gold were buried if they let him pass.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet say when he heard Suhayb's story?
options: That Suhayb had lost everything foolishly
That Suhayb had made a profitable deal
That Suhayb should have fought them
That Suhayb should return for his money
quiz.explanation: The Prophet reportedly smiled and said that Suhayb had made a profitable deal.

quiz.question: What was Suhayb chosen to do in his old age?
options: Lead the community in prayer during political uncertainty
quiz.explanation: In old age, he was chosen to lead the community in prayer during a moment of political uncertainty.

title: A Radio Segment on Asma, the Woman of Two Belts
script: Radio Host: [cheerfully] Good morning, listeners! Today we're discussing Asma bint Abu Bakr, a companion known for her nerve under pressure. We have a caller. Hello!
Caller: [a little nervous] Hello! Thank you for taking my call. I've admired Asma's courage since I first read about her.
Radio Host: [warmly] Wonderful! Can you explain why she earned the unusual nickname, the woman of two belts?
Caller: [thoughtful] Gladly. During the migration, she needed to carry food and supplies for her father, but she had nothing suitable to tie the bundles.
Radio Host: [curious] So what did she do about that problem?
Caller: [explaining] She simply cut her own belt into two pieces, using one to fasten the supplies and the other to keep wearing her clothing properly.
Radio Host: [interested] That's resourceful. Was she involved in anything riskier during that same period?
Caller: [reflective] Yes, actually. She was pregnant at the time, yet she still delivered food secretly to her father and the Prophet, hiding in a cave.
Radio Host: [surprised] Delivering supplies while pregnant sounds physically exhausting, not to mention dangerous if she had been discovered.
Caller: [nodding] It certainly was, and if Quraysh soldiers had caught her, the consequences could have been severe, given how desperately they wanted to find her father.
Radio Host: [tense] Did anyone actually confront her about what she was doing?
Caller: [firmly] Abu Jahl himself came to her house once, demanding to know where her father was hiding, and even struck her when she refused to answer.
Radio Host: [amazed] She refused to answer even Abu Jahl directly? That level of composure is genuinely remarkable.
Caller: [warmly] Exactly, and despite the danger surrounding her family constantly, she remained calm, later living a long life full of similar quiet strength.
Radio Host: [reflective] It sounds like her courage was never loud or dramatic, just steady and reliable whenever it truly mattered.
Caller: [sincerely] That's precisely it. Thank you for letting me share her story this morning.

quiz.question: Why was Asma called the woman of two belts?
options: She wore two belts for fashion
She cut her belt in two to tie supplies during the migration
quiz.explanation: She cut her own belt into two pieces, using one to fasten supplies and the other to keep wearing her clothing properly.

quiz.question: What did Asma do while pregnant during the migration period?
options: She secretly delivered food to her father and the Prophet in a cave
She refused to help her family
quiz.explanation: She was pregnant at the time yet still delivered food secretly to her father and the Prophet, hiding in a cave.

quiz.question: What did Abu Jahl do when he confronted Asma?
options: He struck her when she refused to reveal her father's location
quiz.explanation: Abu Jahl demanded to know where her father was hiding and struck her when she refused to answer.

quiz.question: How did Asma respond to Abu Jahl's demand?
quiz.explanation: She refused to answer even Abu Jahl directly, showing remarkable composure.

quiz.question: How does the caller describe Asma's courage overall?
options: Steady and reliable whenever it truly mattered
quiz.explanation: The caller says her courage was never loud or dramatic, just steady and reliable whenever it truly mattered.

title: The Man No One Wanted to Marry
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Julaybib had no known family, no wealth, and, according to accounts, an appearance that most people in Madinah considered unattractive.
Narrator: [reflective] As a result, whenever marriage was mentioned, families quietly avoided him, assuming someone with so little status could offer their daughters nothing worthwhile.
Narrator: [warmly] The Prophet, however, saw him differently, and one day he asked a respected family whether they would consider Julaybib for their daughter.
Narrator: [tense] The father initially hesitated and began listing reasons to refuse, clearly uncomfortable with such an unexpected and, to him, unsuitable proposal.
Narrator: [with feeling] Before he could finish speaking, though, his daughter interrupted from another room, asking whether the Prophet himself had chosen this match personally.
Narrator: [calm] When her father confirmed that he had, she said she would never reject anyone the Prophet considered worthy, whatever others might think of him.
Narrator: [with wonder] Her answer settled the matter immediately, and the marriage that almost everyone else had dismissed was arranged without further hesitation or complaint.
Narrator: [reflective] If she had judged Julaybib only by wealth or appearance, as her father initially had, this story might have ended in quiet rejection.
Narrator: [warmly] Instead, their marriage reportedly became a genuinely happy one, built on something sturdier than the surface qualities society usually values most.
Narrator: [serious] Not long afterward, Julaybib was killed in battle, and his body was found surrounded by several enemy fighters he had defeated before falling.
Narrator: [sadly] When the Prophet searched for him among the dead, he reportedly said that Julaybib was from him, and he was from Julaybib.
Narrator: [with feeling] He then carried the body himself, ensuring this man once considered unworthy of marriage was honored with the Prophet's own hands.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Even though society had overlooked Julaybib his entire life, both his wife and the Prophet ultimately recognized a worth that others simply failed to see.
Narrator: [warmly] I return to his story whenever I catch myself judging someone too quickly, because true value rarely announces itself at first glance.

quiz.question: Why did families in Madinah avoid marrying their daughters to Julaybib?
options: He had no family, no wealth, and an unattractive appearance
quiz.explanation: Julaybib had no known family, no wealth, and an appearance most people considered unattractive.

quiz.question: What did the father initially do when the Prophet suggested the marriage?
options: He hesitated and began listing reasons to refuse
quiz.explanation: The father initially hesitated and began listing reasons to refuse the unexpected proposal.

quiz.question: Why did the daughter agree to marry Julaybib?
options: Because the Prophet himself had chosen the match
Because she had no other options
quiz.explanation: She said she would never reject anyone the Prophet considered worthy, once she learned he had chosen the match.

quiz.question: How was Julaybib found after the battle?
options: Surrounded by several enemy fighters he had defeated
quiz.explanation: His body was found surrounded by several enemy fighters he had defeated before falling.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet reportedly say when he found Julaybib?
options: That Julaybib was from him, and he was from Julaybib
That the marriage had been a mistake
quiz.explanation: The Prophet reportedly said that Julaybib was from him, and he was from Julaybib, then carried the body himself.
